scope: Values the screen carries, each with how far it was read on 4 November 2026. Search summaries are second-hand; recalled values were not re-read in this study and stay open until checked.

sources.citation: Parker, Wilcock, Paola, Dietrich & Pitlick (2007), JGR Earth Surface 112, F04005
sources.use: Gravel-bed bankfull relations H = 0.382 Q^0.4 g^-0.2, B = 4.63 Q^0.4 g^-0.2 Qhat^0.0667, S = 0.101 Qhat^-0.344, Qhat = Q/(sqrt(gD) D^2); the width relation also used for sand beds (an extrapolation)
sources.read: Equations read as reproduced in Palucis & Lamb (2017, GRL 44, eqs 8-10, extracted text); coefficients confirmed by a search summary; the paper itself not opened (publisher refused)

sources.citation: Palucis & Lamb (2017), What controls channel form in steep mountain streams? GRL 44
sources.use: Source text for Parker et al. (2007) relations
sources.read: Relevant section read (extracted PDF text)

sources.citation: Wilkerson & Parker (2011), J. Hydraulic Engineering 137(7), 739-753
sources.use: Bankfull Shields number of single-thread sand-bed rivers falls as Rep^-1/2 (D50 0.062-0.5 mm)
sources.read: Search summaries of the abstract; fitted coefficients not obtained (paywalled), open

sources.citation: Trampush, Huzurbazar & McElroy (2014), Water Resources Research 50, 9211-9220
sources.use: Bankfull Shields number 17 Rep^-1/2 from the global compilation of single-thread rivers
sources.read: Read second-hand in Hayden et al. (2019) eq. 11 (extracted text)

sources.citation: Hayden, Lamb et al. (2019), sinuous ridges by inversion of river-channel belts, with implications for Mars (Icarus)
sources.use: Carries the Trampush/Wilkerson-Parker closure to another gravity in dimensionless form
sources.read: Methods section read (extracted PDF text)

sources.citation: Dunne & Jerolmack (2020), What sets river width? Science Advances 6, eabc1505
sources.use: Bankfull stress near 1.2 times the critical stress of the most resistant material lining the channel (18 sections, none above 1.5); fine-grained rivers depart from the Shields curve at about 10 Pa, where cohesive banks exceed the bed
sources.read: Search summary of the paper

sources.citation: Ferguson & Church (2004), Journal of Sedimentary Research 74, 933-937
sources.use: Settling law w = R g D^2 / (C1 nu + sqrt(0.75 C2 R g D^3)), C1 = 18, C2 = 1 for natural grains
sources.read: Search summary (constants); equation form standard, checked against Stokes and a 2.5 cm/s medium sand in the tests

sources.citation: Akiyama & Stefan (1984), J. Hydraulic Engineering 110, 484-497; Parker & Toniolo (2007), J. Hydraulic Engineering 133
sources.use: Plunging at a densimetric Froude number of about 0.5 (0.4-0.8 reported), plunge depth (q^2 / (g' Fp^2))^(1/3)
sources.read: Search summaries (turbulence-resolving plunging studies citing both)

sources.citation: Mulder & Syvitski (1995), Journal of Geology 103, 285-299
sources.use: River water needs 36-43 kg/m3 of sediment to plunge into seawater (the brief's figure)
sources.read: Not read in this study; reproduced by calculation, 41.8 kg/m3 at 25 C

sources.citation: Nienhuis, Ashton, Edmonds, Hoitink, Kettner, Rowland & Tornqvist (2020), Nature 577, 514-518
sources.use: Qwave as max - min of the angular wave energy convolved with deep-water alongshore transport (eq. 1); Qtide = Qw,tide Qriver / Qw,river (eq. 2) with Qw,tide = 1/2 omega k a^2 (d_u/S)^2 beta (eq. 3); a delta is dominated by the largest of the three fluxes (eq. 4)
sources.read: Methods read in full in the author manuscript (extracted text)

sources.citation: Ashton & Murray (2006), JGR Earth Surface 111, F04011
sources.use: CERC recast into deep-water terms, Q ~ H0^(12/5) T^(1/5) cos^(6/5) sin; K2 here derived with g explicit
sources.read: Recalled; derivation in physics.longshore_max

sources.citation: US Army Corps of Engineers (1984), Shore Protection Manual
sources.use: CERC K = 0.39 with significant height; JONSWAP fetch-limited growth and fully developed limits
sources.read: Recalled standard values; the growth law is checked against the wave study's computed seas

sources.citation: Edmonds & Slingerland (2007), JGR Earth Surface 112, F02034
sources.use: Distance to the mouth bar rises with the jet's momentum flux over the grains' weight to about the 1/5 power
sources.read: Abstract via search summary; the 3-width coefficient (2-6) is a design guess, open

sources.citation: Jerolmack & Mohrig (2007), Geology 35, 463-466
sources.use: Avulsion time T_A = h / v_A with v_A the near-channel aggradation; avulsion at a superelevation of about one channel depth
sources.read: Relevant text read (extracted PDF)

sources.citation: Ganti, Chadwick, Hassenruck-Gudipati, Fuller & Lamb (2016), Science Advances 2, e1501768
sources.use: Avulsion length scales with the backwater length h_c / S within a factor of 2
sources.read: Introduction and Fig. 1 read (extracted text)

sources.citation: Crosato & Mosselman (2009), Water Resources Research 45, W03424
sources.use: Bar mode m^2 = 0.17 g (b - 3) B^3 S / (sqrt(Delta D50) C Q), b = 4 sand (mixed load), 10 gravel; m about 1 alternate bars, 2 central bars, 3 and more braided
sources.read: Symbols and b values from search summaries; the equation's form recalled and checked for dimensional consistency only, open

sources.citation: Grant (1997), Critical flow constrains flow hydraulics in mobile-bed streams: a new hypothesis, Water Resources Research 33(2), 349-358
sources.use: The bound that mobile-bed channels hold their flow near critical (Froude number about 1) at most, against which the screened slopes' bankfull Froude numbers of 1.7-1.9 read as too steep
sources.read: Abstract via search summary (4 November 2026); used for its qualitative bound only

sources.citation: Alberts et al. (1995), WEPP technical documentation
sources.use: Bare-soil critical shear 2.67 + 0.065 clay% - 0.058 VFS% Pa (soils with 30% sand or more)
sources.read: Reused from the storm-water study (repository); extrapolated here to the clay texture

sources.citation: Wynn & Mostaghimi (2006) and related jet-test studies of rooted banks
sources.use: Roots raise banks' critical shear; root factor 1.5-6 taken as a design bracket
sources.read: Search results only, not read; open

sources.citation: Carrier (2003), J. Geotechnical and Geoenvironmental Engineering 129, 956-959
sources.use: Lunar soil median 72 um (40-130 um), Cu 8.7-30, 90% of the mass between 10 um and 1 mm
sources.read: Search summaries

sources.use: Regolith texture and density (repository's existing source)
sources.read: Reused from the repository's sources

sources.use: Plowed fields erode 1-2 orders of magnitude faster than ground under native vegetation (medians above 1 mm a year)
sources.read: Abstract via search summary (the steering's one Earth review of bare against covered ground)

sources.citation: Goldberg & Forsythe-type flocculation measurements (USDA ARS reprint P1095, Flocculation of reference clays and arid-zone soil clays) and related studies
sources.use: Critical flocculation of smectite, beidellite and illite at 5-25 mmol/L of monovalent salt; about 3 mM CaCl2 for montmorillonite; about 100 mmol/L NaCl at alkaline pH
sources.read: Search summaries only; the calcium bracket 0.3-3 mmol/L and the organic flocculation bracket are design values, open (no review read)
